mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 7.5% for two consecutive months, it signals persistent labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5% for two consecutive months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown in consumer and business sectors, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and INDPRO (measured as product of deviations from 3-month moving averages) fails to predict negative returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or mean 60-day return not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary normalization regimes (FEDFUNDS > 0.15% and rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.15% and rising (3-month change > 0.05%), or mean return not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior 3 months indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS increases over the prior 3 months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in the residential sector that reduces consumer confidence and business investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 1000 for two consecutive months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in retail sales (RSAFS) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflationary pressures that reduce corporate profit margins and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between RSAFS and CPIAUCSL (measured as product of deviations from 3-month moving averages) fails to predict negative returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or mean 60-day return not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During industrial contraction regimes (INDPRO < 99.0 and falling), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days as manufacturing slowdowns reduce corporate earnings and investment.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 99.0 and falling (3-month change < -0.5%), or mean return not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
